title: Paloma and the Aftermath
premise: Elias Vann, a Portuguese-to-English translator who has forgotten more of his mother tongue than he can admit, attends the funeral of a client and is mistaken for family by a stranger who calls him by a name nobody in the Almeida household uses. The name belongs to Tomás, his grandfather — the man in the old photographs who abandoned Astrid Almeida's family decades ago after a betrayal that was never spoken aloud, only inherited. As the Almeida house is prepared for sale, Elias stays on as an accidental archivist of their grief, translating letters his grandfather left behind that reveal the betrayal was an act of desperate justice outside the law. In the end, Elias reads the final letter aloud in the emptied house, forgiving the stranger in the photographs — and being forgiven in turn — before the keys change hands.
about_author: Theo Lockridge is the pen name of a former court interpreter who spent fifteen years listening to other people's truths before writing his own. He lives near the coast, where he collects untranslatable words and the stories attached to them.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Word
chapters.summary: Elias, mid-translation of a dying novelist's manuscript, loses a word he has known since childhood and feels himself thinning into English. A summons arrives: the funeral of Marisa Almeida, his last client. POV Elias. Emotional beat: quiet dread of erasure, the sense of living as a tenant in one's own life.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: At the funeral, an elderly stranger grips Elias's hand and calls him Tomás. Astrid Almeida, the daughter, goes white — Tomás is the man in the photograph above the mantel, face turned away. Elias does not correct anyone. POV Elias. Emotional beat: vertigo of mistaken identity becoming chosen identity.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid asks him to stay through the estate sale — not as family, she insists, but because the house needs emptying and she cannot do it alone. Rooms hold objects labeled in three generations of handwriting. POV alternating Elias and Astrid. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people guarding different wounds.

chapters.title: Letters in a Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Elias finds a locked drawer in the study; Astrid produces a key her mother hid in a sewing tin. Inside: letters in old Portuguese, written by Tomás to Marisa, never sent. Elias begins translating them against his own resistance. POV Elias. Emotional beat: compulsion and shame intertwined.

chapters.title: What the Village Knew
chapters.summary: The first translated letter reveals 1963: Tomás reported a neighbor's crime to authorities outside any lawful channel, protecting Marisa's sister and damning his own standing. Astrid reads over his shoulder and recoils — her family's version makes Tomás the villain. POV Astrid. Emotional beat: the ground of inherited memory cracking.

chapters.title: Two Versions of One Man
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Elias with her mother's diary, which names Tomás as the thief of the family's land. Elias defends a grandfather he barely knew, and their argument turns personal — she accuses him of trespassing on grief he hasn't earned. POV Astrid. Emotional beat: rising tension, intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: The Sale
chapters.summary: The buyer's agent schedules the closing; boxes multiply; Astrid grows brittle and sleepless. Elias discovers a final letter hidden inside the lining of a suitcase, sealed, addressed 'to whoever is left.' He cannot yet bring himself to open it. POV Elias. Emotional beat: deadline pressure compressing everything unsaid.

chapters.title: Sealed
chapters.summary: Elias opens the letter alone at night: Tomás confesses fully — the land was taken to pay a debt that would have destroyed them all, and he chose exile so the family could hate one man instead of fracturing. He asks forgiveness from no one, only remembrance. POV Elias. Emotional beat: devastating clarity, grief for a stranger who was never strange.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: On the morning of the closing, with the house bare and the buyers' car in the drive, Elias reads Tomás's letter aloud to Astrid in Portuguese, then again in his own halting translation. She hears her mother's silence explained at last. POV alternating. Emotional beat: climax — confession, fury, and the beginning of release.

chapters.title: Owner of Nothing, Keeper of This
chapters.summary: Astrid signs the papers but keeps the letters and the photograph, turning Tomás's face toward the room. She gives Elias a word from his lost childhood that she'd written down years ago from Marisa's stories. They part at the gate, no longer strangers. POV Elias. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging restored not by blood or law, but by witness.
